newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Comalco sees better aluminium demand.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Comalco sees better aluminium demand.

text.p: Bauxite miner and alumina and aluminium producer Comalco Ltd said on Monday that it expected demand for aluminium to improve slightly in 1997 and that there was potential for improved price stability.
"Demand for aluminium is expected to improve slightly in 1997, but this will depend on economic recovery in Europe and continued growth in the United States," Comalco said.
It said experience in the first two months confirmed this.
"Consumption in Asia is not expected to grow in 1997," it said.
Comalco said demand for bauxite this year was expected to remain at similar levels to 1996.
"International alumina prices are expected to improve from the low levels experienced in mid-1997."
Less price volatility in the aluminium price hinges on London Metal Exchange (LME) inventories staying above 500,000 tonnes, Comalco said.
"Providing LME stocks do not fall below 500,000 tonnes this year, the aluminium industry may expect a less volatile price cycle," Comalco said.
The market showed signs of achieving equilibrium in the seconbd half of 1996 and this is expected to continue through 1997, the company said.
"This equilibrium may provide a foundation for improved price stability," Comalco said.
Comalco said it made headway in its smelter expansion and upgrading programmes in 1996.

"In 1996, our share of output was 476,000 tonnes of aluminium and this year, following the completion of the Tiwai point smelter upgrade and the commissioning of line three at Boyne Island, it will be well over 500,000 tonnes," the company said.

The first aluminium from a third potline being installed at the Boyne Island, Queensland complex is expected to commence production in May and be in full production by the end of the year, the company said.
Comalco said it was continuing investigations into a new alumina refinery and is taking steps to improve its Weipa bauxite operations.
"All these steps are consistent with our strategy of focussing on mining, refining and smelting operations," Comalco said.
Demand for bauxite this year is expected to remain at similar levels to 1996, while international alumina prices are seen improving, Comalco said.
Production of bauxite from the Weipa mine, at 9.5 million tonnes, was an improvement on 1995's figure of 8.9 million tonnes, Comalco said.
Since September 1996, bauxite mining has been concentrated in the Andoom mining area, due to changes to the grade of bauxite supplied to major customers.
Mining operations are being restructured, it said.
Sales of calcined bauxite were below 1995 but should recover in 1997 given stronger European economic performance, it said.
The Queensland Alumina Lt (QAL) and Eurallumina refineries achieved record production, it said.
Cost improvement programmes at both refineries led to increased efficiencies, Comalco said.
QAL is implementing further productivity improvements to reduce costs and lift production capacity from 3.3 million tonnes in 1996 to over 3.6 million tonnes in 1998, it said.
Alumina sales were higher than in 1995, with increased alumina demand from the upgraded Tiwai Point smelter and the Bell Bay smelter's return to full capacity, Comalco said.
"Although the international market for alumina remained in relatively close balance, the lower primary aluminium price led to reduced alumina spot prices and sales volumes," Comalco said.
